<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as winter squash

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers winter squash in 4 forms kept separate in every comparison: winter squash, as sold (213 results), winter squash, cooked (16 results), winter squash, flour or meal (11 results) and winter squash, oil (7 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-winter-squash" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-winter-squash-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of winter squash, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach winter squash

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>

<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach winter squash comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Winter squash, as sold from evening purchase had lead higher at 840 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dada AO, Makanjuola BC, Adewumi MO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Level of Heavy Metals in Commonly Consumed Leafy Vegetables Sold in Major Markets within Ibadan Metropolis, South Western, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environment Pollution and Human Health 12(2):24-30</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Winter squash, cooked (market samples, Konya Province, Turkey (2021 products)) had lead higher at 668 µg/kg, against 288 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (winter squash, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dada AO, Makanjuola BC, Adewumi MO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Level of Heavy Metals in Commonly Consumed Leafy Vegetables Sold in Major Markets within Ibadan Metropolis, South Western, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environment Pollution and Human Health 12(2):24-30</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Every source record that names winter squash was decided on its content: 26 occurrence extracted, 26 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

## Winter squash FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-winter-squash" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-winter-squash" data-question="What heavy metals are found in winter squash?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in winter squash?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-winter-squash" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-winter-squash" data-question="How do heavy metals get into winter squash?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into winter squash?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, winter squash from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than winter squash from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dada AO, Makanjuola BC, Adewumi MO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Level of Heavy Metals in Commonly Consumed Leafy Vegetables Sold in Major Markets within Ibadan Metropolis, South Western, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environment Pollution and Human Health 12(2):24-30</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Winter squash, as sold from evening purchase had lead higher at 840 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dada AO, Makanjuola BC, Adewumi MO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Level of Heavy Metals in Commonly Consumed Leafy Vegetables Sold in Major Markets within Ibadan Metropolis, South Western, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environment Pollution and Human Health 12(2):24-30</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dada2024-ibadan-market-leafy-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-winter-squash-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-winter-squash-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of winter squash have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of winter squash have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for winter squash, cooked (1.6 µg/kg) and highest for winter squash, as sold (3 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-winter-squash" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-winter-squash" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in winter squash?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in winter squash?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, winter squash, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1.3 µg/kg) and the highest in AFRO (70 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (3 µg/kg) and the highest in AFRO (350 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-winter-squash" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-winter-squash" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in winter squash?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in winter squash?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same winter squash.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Winter squash, cooked (market samples, Konya Province, Turkey (2021 products)) had lead higher at 668 µg/kg, against 288 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (winter squash, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-winter-squash-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-winter-squash-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in winter squash is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in winter squash is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 4 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007; 2: 88-94</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Laizu 2007 reported inorganic arsenic at 700 µg/kg (mean ± 600 SD) in winter squash, as sold from fruiting vegetables, local market, Dhaka.<sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007;
